lines.li: [them,their:tribal] Since you broke that camp, our hunters walk the old trails again.
[them,their:hightech] Since you broke that camp, our caravans take the short road again.
[them] Since your people broke that camp, our carts use that road again.
[us] That camp was a danger to us too.
[them,their:empire] The Empire keeps note of such things, and so do I.
[them] Still, it was your people who went out there.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} use the road again since the colony broke a raiders' camp that troubled it.

lines.li: [them] That {DEEDNAME} you broke had my people afraid to travel.
[us] We didn't like it much either.
[them] We sat behind our walls and hoped, and your people went out.
[them] I came here the short way, past where that camp of raiders stood.
[us] Quiet now?
[them] Quiet as a grave, which is how a trader likes a road.
[them] My people talk about your colony differently since that camp was broken.
[us] Differently how?
[them,their:tribal] As people who keep the paths safe, not strangers who live near them.
[them] As neighbors, not as strangers who happen to live nearby.
[us] I'll take that.
[them] Take it, it's meant.
[them] I let my children out past the fields again, now that camp is gone.
[us] Good.
[them] It is, you don't know how good.
[them] First that camp, and now raiders at your walls again, it's a hard time for you.
[us] We're still standing.
[them] That's what my people like about you.
[them] The elders say a camp of thieves is a thorn in the foot, and your people pulled it.
[us] It took some pulling.
[them] Thorns do, and the foot remembers who did it.
[them] Brigands on the roads are an insult to the Empire, and your colony removed one.
[us] We removed it for our own sake.
[them] The court will not mind the reason.
[them,their:tribal] Our warriors burned that camp near you, and they sing about it at every fire.
[them,their:medieval] Our riders burned that camp near you, and they bring it up at every supper.
[them,their:industrial] Our patrol burned that camp near you, and they've been insufferable since.
[them,their:spacer] Our strike team burned that camp near you, and filed a very long report on it.
[them] Our people burned that camp near you, and they're proud of it.
[us] We're grateful.
[them] Tell them yourself next time, they'd like to hear it from you.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} burned a raiders' camp near the colony.

lines.li: [them] Allies keep each other's roads clear, that's why our people burned that camp.
[us] We owe you for it.
[them] You do, and we'll remember it when the road is ours.
[them] I'm too old to have gone with them when ours burned that camp near you.
[us] Would you have wanted to?
[them] Every old fighter wants to, and every one of us is glad of a warm bed instead.
[us] Your people made camp near us once, to raid us.
[them] Not all of us, and not with my blessing.
[us] Still, they were yours.
[them,their:tribal] The elders argued about it for a whole moon.
[them] Some of us said so at the time, for what that was worth.
[them] I know what our people did near your walls, you needn't remind me.
[us] I wasn't going to.
[them] There's no getting round it, your people broke our people's camp.
[us] Then we understand each other.
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] We do, and I'd rather neither side did it that way again.
[them] We do, and that's about all.
[them] Your people broke our camp, and not all of ours came home from it.
[us] They came to raid us.
[them] I know why they came, I'm telling you what it cost.
[them] We remember the {WRONGNAME} your people broke.
[us] So do we, it was raiding us.
[them] I hear our camp near you gave up in the end, and your walls held.
[us] They held.
[them,their:tribal] Then the spirits were with you, and not with them.
[them] Then they should have stayed at home, and I said so.
[them] Some of our people camped near you once, and your colony paid them to go.
[us] It was cheaper than a war.
[them,their:rough] Then it was silver well spent, on both sides.
[them] I'm not proud of it, but I'm glad it ended that way.
[them] Your colony paid our people to leave it alone once, and they still laugh about it.
[us] Let them laugh, we're still here.
[them] When the peace came, our fighters near you struck their camp and came home.
[us] We were glad of it.
[them,their:tribal] So were they, there was hunting to be done.
[them] So were they, most of them had fields to see to.
[them] My people say you were one of those who went out to that camp.
[us] There were a few of us.
[them,their:tribal] A few is how every good story at the fire begins.
[them] A few is enough to remember by name.
[them] You're one of the ones who broke that camp, I owe you a drink at least.
[us] I'll hold you to it.
[them,their:tribal] Hold me to it at the next full moon, then.
[them] Do, I'm good for it.
